script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this is form only, not a book number. Detroit has the heavier skill volume (Gibbs 45.0 carries/208 rush yards, St. Brown 27.0 targets/209 rec yards) while the Jets have allowed 1 pass of 20+ yards on 67 attempts and 4.09 rush YPC, so the base read is a Detroit-leaning game with explosives capped and Gibbs keeping a large carry share. pre_mortem: Hall loses if the Jets fall behind, Allen (15.0 carries, 47 yards) and Geno Smith (8.0 carries, 27 yards) take the early-down work, his 3.45 YPC never jumps toward Detroit's 5.12 allowed, and the 79 receiving yards on 7 targets do not repeat, leaving him under 86 combined. Williams loses if Detroit trails and Goff (0.33 EPA vs blitz, n=23) hits one 40-plus shot out of the 177 air yards already aimed at him. The Hall counter needs a blowout pass-only script; the 43% blitz and 2 air-yard receiving role are why the combined line was taken instead of rush yards over 60. The Williams counter is one-play variance, not the two-game usage trend (78 yards on 13 targets). Neither counter is stronger than the read.
slip_story: One matchup story, not a shootout stack: Detroit's run and blitz bleed feeds Hall rushrecyds over, and the Jets' explosive-pass lid feeds Jameson Williams recyds under. Both survive the base script and the Detroit-leads clock-kill flip; the shootout flip is what kills the Williams leg. Do not pair with Wilson or St. Brown overs, which need Detroit's 10 explosives and 13.27 middle YPA, or with any total that is not in the pack.
